directive.name: design
directive.description: Enforce Linear-inspired design standards and guide senior-designer-quality UX/UI decision-making for new features. Uses Shadcn/Vue components with OKLCH design tokens. Prioritizes minimal, intentional interfaces over feature-heavy hobby engineering.

context.principle: Reduce visual noise ruthlessly. Every element must earn its place. Linear's philosophy: "small points of friction don't just add up, they multiply." Remove borders, reduce contrast between elements, use subtle separators.
Every design decision must have a reason. Before adding any UI element, ask: "What user problem does this solve?" If you cannot articulate the answer, the element should not exist.
Token-only styling. Never use raw Tailwind values like bg-red-500 or px-6. All visual decisions trace back to design tokens in style.css. This ensures consistency and enables theming.
Dark-first design. Linear uses dark gray on black as the primary aesthetic. Design for dark mode first, then adapt for light. Ensure sufficient contrast for readability without harsh brightness.
High information density with breathing room. Linear achieves density through careful typography and consistent spacing, not cramming. Use whitespace to create visual hierarchy, not decoration.
Prefer existing Shadcn components over custom solutions. Before creating anything new, check components/ui/ for existing primitives. Compose complex UIs from simple, tested building blocks.

Think like a senior designer, not a hobby engineer. Senior designers: - Question requirements before implementing - Consider edge cases and error states upfront - Propose alternatives when requirements are unclear - Validate assumptions with user workflows - Reject feature creep that harms UX

process.rule: RESEARCH BEFORE DESIGNING. For any new UI feature: 1. Identify 2-3 comparable products (Linear, Notion, Figma, etc.) 2. Note how they solve similar problems 3. Document patterns that align with our minimal aesthetic 4. Propose options with tradeoffs, not single solutions

MAP USER WORKFLOWS. Before designing any interface: 1. List the jobs-to-be-done this feature enables 2. Identify the primary action (what do users do 80% of the time?) 3. Consider keyboard-first interaction patterns 4. Plan error states and edge cases explicitly

PROPOSE THREE OPTIONS when UX choices are non-trivial: - Option A: Minimal change (progressive enhancement) - Option B: Moderate redesign (balanced approach) - Option C: Ideal solution (if no constraints existed) Document tradeoffs and recommend one with justification.

USE SEMANTIC TOKEN CLASSES. Map Tailwind to tokens: - Colors: bg-background, text-foreground, bg-muted, text-muted-foreground - Borders: border-border, border-input - Interactive: bg-primary, bg-secondary, bg-accent, bg-destructive - Never: bg-gray-800, text-white, border-zinc-700

COMPONENT COMPOSITION HIERARCHY: 1. Use raw Shadcn components from components/ui/ unchanged 2. Create wrapper components in components/ for product-level patterns 3. Never modify components/ui/ files directly - extend via wrappers 4. Document non-obvious component choices in code comments

INTERACTION PATTERNS following Linear: - Keyboard shortcuts for power users (document in UI) - Hover states that reveal secondary actions - Transitions: 150ms ease-out for micro-interactions - Focus rings using ring token for accessibility - Loading states that preserve layout (skeleton, not spinner)

VALIDATE DESIGN DECISIONS during review: - Does every element serve a clear purpose? - Are tokens used consistently (no raw values)? - Do error states exist and follow the same visual language? - Is the feature keyboard-navigable? - Does it maintain density without feeling cramped?

When fixing design issues, trace back to principles: - Visual inconsistency? Check token usage (C3) - Cluttered interface? Apply noise reduction (C1) - Confusing interaction? Revisit user workflow (P2) - Missing state? Add error/loading/empty states

check.reason: Raw Tailwind color values violate token-only styling (C3). Use semantic tokens: bg-background, text-foreground, bg-muted, bg-destructive, etc.
Consider using consistent spacing patterns. Prefer Shadcn component defaults or establish explicit spacing tokens.

check.item: All interactive elements have visible focus states
Error states are designed, not afterthoughts
Loading states preserve layout (no layout shift)
Empty states provide guidance (not just "No items")
Hover states reveal secondary actions appropriately
Text contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body text)
Icons have text labels or aria-labels
Comparable products researched for complex features

example.explanation: Uses raw color values (gray-900, blue-600) instead of semantic tokens. Breaks theming and consistency.
Uses semantic tokens (bg-card, border-border) and Shadcn Button variants. Supports theming automatically.

example.code:
User: "Add a settings panel"
LLM: "I'll add a settings panel with tabs for General, Appearance, and Notifications..."
[Immediately starts implementing without research or options]
example.explanation: Jumps to implementation without understanding requirements, researching patterns, or proposing options. Hobby engineer approach.

example.code:
User: "Add a settings panel"
LLM: "Before implementing, let me understand the requirements:
**Research:** Linear uses a modal with categorized sections. Notion uses a full-page layout. VS Code uses a searchable list.
**Questions:** - What settings need to be configurable? - How frequently will users access settings? - Should settings sync across devices?
**Options:** A) Dropdown menu (minimal, quick access, limited space) B) Modal dialog (Linear-style, focused, doesn't leave context) C) Dedicated page (extensive settings, searchable)
**Recommendation:** Option B - modal dialog. Matches our minimal aesthetic and keeps users in context. Appropriate for ~10-20 settings.
Should I proceed with Option B, or would you prefer a different approach?"
example.explanation: Researches comparable products, asks clarifying questions, proposes options with tradeoffs, and recommends with justification. Senior designer approach.

example.code: <!-- WRONG: Visual noise --> <Card class="border-2 shadow-lg"> <CardHeader class="border-b bg-muted"> <CardTitle class="text-lg font-bold underline"> Task Details </CardTitle> </CardHeader> <CardContent class="border-t"> <Badge variant="outline" class="border-2">Status</Badge> </CardContent> </Card>
example.explanation: Multiple borders, heavy shadows, underlined text, thick badge borders - visual noise that doesn't serve a purpose.
Uses Shadcn defaults. No extra borders or decorations. Every element serves its purpose without visual noise.
No handling for loading, empty, or error states. Users see nothing or broken UI in edge cases.
Handles loading (skeleton), error (retry action), empty (guidance), and success states. Professional, complete implementation.
